lead: A wireless LAN joins phones and laptops over radio instead of cable. IEEE 802.11 (Wi-Fi) shares one channel politely: stations listen, wait and back off before sending, so collisions are avoided, not detected. Bluetooth is the opposite: one master tightly controls a small piconet of slaves. Both replace the last few metres of cable — a campus hotspot, a Chennai coffee shop, earbuds paired to a phone.
prereq: You need the access-network part of Chapter 1.1.

sections.h3: 802.11 architecture: stations, APs and service sets

blocks.text: A station (STA) is a device with a wireless network card. An access point (AP) is a fixed box that bridges the radio channel to the wired network.
A basic service set (BSS) is one AP plus the stations joined to it. A BSS with no AP is independent — an ad hoc network, covered in Chapter 1.8.

An extended service set (ESS) joins two or more BSSs through a distribution system (DS), usually wired Ethernet. The DS forwards frames between APs, so a user walks from one classroom to the next and stays on the same network. The service set identifier (SSID) is the Wi-Fi name you pick from the list; inside an ESS the same name is also called the ESSID.

sections.h3: Two layers and the join procedure

blocks.text: 802.11 defines two layers. The physical layer (PHY) turns bits into radio: direct-sequence spread spectrum (DSSS) in 802.11b, orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) from 802.11a and 802.11g onward. The MAC layer decides who transmits next, adds addresses and a checksum.

items: Scan: listen for beacon frames; an AP beacons about every 100 ms with its SSID and data rates.
Probe and authenticate: send a probe request, then exchange authentication frames.
Associate: the AP accepts the station and returns an association ID (AID); data frames follow.

blocks.text: Ethernet uses CSMA/CD — listen, send, and detect collisions while sending. A radio cannot hear itself transmit, so 802.11 uses CSMA/CA: carrier sense multiple access with collision avoidance.

A station with a frame waits until the channel is idle for a DIFS (DCF interframe space). It then counts a random backoff down in idle slots, freezing the counter when the channel goes busy. At zero it transmits, and the receiver replies with an ACK after a SIFS (short interframe space). Since SIFS < DIFS, the ACK grabs the channel before other stations can start.

blocks.where: CW is the contention window in slots, starting at 15 or 31 and doubling to 1023 after each failure; slot is 9 µs or 20 µs depending on the PHY.

blocks.text: Hidden nodes: A and C both reach AP B but not each other, so both may transmit and collide at B. With RTS/CTS the sender asks using a request-to-send frame, B answers with clear-to-send, and every station that hears the CTS keeps quiet for that exchange.
Bluetooth is a short-range (about 10 m) cable replacement for earbuds, keyboards and car audio. A piconet is one master and up to seven active slaves sharing a channel.

The master polls one slave at a time, so the link is time-division duplex with no collisions. The channel hops 1600 times a second over 79 channels of 1 MHz in the 2.4 GHz band (frequency-hopping spread spectrum, FHSS), which dodges interference from Wi-Fi and microwave ovens.

A device that belongs to two piconets at once links them; the linked piconets together form a scatternet. The link manager handles link setup, power and security, while a profile states what a use case needs, such as hands-free audio or a serial port.
HIPERLAN/2 and wireless ATM were rival broadband wireless systems; both are now history.

figure.caption: One 1500-byte frame timed on the air: the data block lasts 1.09 ms and the second block, preamble plus ACK, DIFS and backoff, lasts 0.50 ms, giving 1.59 ms per frame and 68.6 percent efficiency.

spec.aria: A timeline of one 1500-byte frame at 11 Mbps lasting 1.59 ms, split into 1.09 ms of data transmission followed by 0.50 ms of preamble, ACK, DIFS and backoff overhead.

examples.question: An 802.11b network sends 1500-byte data frames at 11 Mbps. Preamble, ACK, DIFS and backoff add 0.50 ms per frame. Find the frame transmission time and the efficiency.
examples.answer: Frame time is 1.09 ms and efficiency is 68.6 percent, so nearly a third of the airtime is overhead.
examples.check:
b = 1500*8
t = b/11e6*1000
tot = t + 0.50
eff = t/tot*100
print(b)
print(round(t,2))
print(round(tot,2))
print(round(eff,1))

traps: Saying Wi-Fi uses CSMA/CD like Ethernet. A radio cannot listen while it transmits, so 802.11 avoids collisions with DIFS, backoff and ACK, plus RTS/CTS for hidden nodes.
Mixing BSS and ESS. A BSS is one AP; an ESS is several BSSs joined by the distribution system.
Forgetting SIFS < DIFS. That short gap is exactly why the ACK goes out before other backoffs expire.
Writing 'one master and eight active slaves'. It is seven active slaves; further devices can be parked.
Swapping the radios: Bluetooth uses FHSS and time-division duplex, while 802.11b uses DSSS with CSMA/CA.

quiz.q: Define BSS, ESS and distribution system.
quiz.a: A BSS is one AP with its stations; an ESS is two or more BSSs joined by a distribution system, the backbone that forwards frames between APs.

quiz.q: State the number of active slaves in a piconet and the hop rate.
quiz.a: Up to seven active slaves under one master; 1600 hops per second over 79 channels of 1 MHz.
A transmitting radio cannot listen to the channel at the same time, because its own signal is far stronger than any incoming one, so collisions cannot be detected and must be avoided instead.

quiz.q: Explain the hidden node problem and the RTS/CTS cure.
quiz.a: Two stations reach the AP but not each other, so both sense an idle channel and collide at the AP. The sender transmits an RTS; the AP answers with a CTS that both stations hear, so the other one stays silent for that exchange.

quiz.q: CW starts at 15 slots and the slot time is 9 µs (OFDM PHY). A station draws backoff = 7. How long does it wait after DIFS?
quiz.a: Wait = 7 × 9 µs = 63 µs of idle slots.

quiz.q: Why does the contention window double after each failed attempt?
quiz.a: A failure means the channel is crowded, so a wider window spreads the retries of all stations over more slots and lowers the chance of another collision. With a fixed small window on a busy channel, collisions repeat and throughput collapses.

beyond: Not for the exam. 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) keeps CSMA/CA with EDCA and adds OFDMA plus AP-triggered uplink scheduling, so one transmission opportunity can carry several stations at once. Bluetooth Low Energy now carries beacons and wearables that classic Bluetooth handled poorly. Both sit under the Android and iOS networking APIs you meet in Unit 5.
